question: Does a 2048 batch/microbatch make the production 35B read prompts 5x+ faster with no loss of graded accuracy?
why: Real Open WebUI requests on Slink spend most of their wall time reading the prompt: engine.log shows 91 s prompt vs 8 s decode over 5 requests, and the first message of a chat waited 26-117 s at ~87-100 tok/s. Production uses batch 256 / microbatch 128 with experts in RAM (labcore.py "balanced" profile).

speed_sweep.tool: prefill.py (cache_prompt off, greedy, 64-token answers, 2 repeats, GLM teacher resident)
speed_sweep.same_greedy_text_as_production: identical at 2675 and 9479 tokens for 1024 and 2048; different at 7362 tokens for every larger microbatch (summation order changes); texts were not saved
speed_sweep.crash: 512/512 crashed on its 4th long request with "CUDA error: an illegal memory access", the same error as COT-EFF-3 arm BC at production settings (batch 256 / microbatch 128). Two crashes in ~350 requests on engine b11146 across two configs, so this is not specific to large batches.

arms.lever: thinking off (the Model Lab default) with batch/microbatch 2048; otherwise identical to COT-EFF-2 arm N

accuracy_check: N2K runs once on the COT-EFF-2 confirmation set (130 items) into the same run directory, so it is paired item by item with arm N (74/130 at batch 256 / microbatch 128). Grading is unchanged.
adoption_rule: Production Model Lab uses batch/microbatch 2048 for the 35B if N2K correct >= N - 2 of 130 with an exact McNemar p > 0.05 (microbatch changes no weights, so any difference is greedy-path noise), AND N2K has no more server crashes than one in 130. Otherwise production stays at 256/128 and the result is reported.
production_change: labcore.py profile change for the 35B, applied at its next load (it is not loaded now; nothing is restarted). Rollback: restore batch 256 / microbatch 128 in the same profile.
